Short-term wind speed prediction based on LMD and improved FA optimized
combined kernel function LSSVM✩
Zhongda Tian

A R T I C L E I N F O
Keywords:
Wind speed prediction
Local mean decomposition
Kernel function
LSSVM
Firefly algorithm
A B S T R A C T
Accurate prediction of wind speed is of great significance to the operation and maintenance of wind farms, the
optimal scheduling of turbines, and the safe and stable operation of power grids. A new prediction method
for short-term wind speed based on local mean decomposition (LMD) and combined kernel function least
squares support vector machine (LSSVM) is proposed. The short-term wind speed time series is decomposed
into some components by the LMD algorithm. Based on LSSVM, radial basis function and the Polynomial
function are used to generate the combined kernel function. The combined kernel function LSSVM combines
the advantages of the radial basis function and the Polynomial function, which can achieve better prediction
accuracy. The decomposed wind speed time series are predicted separately by the combined kernel function
LSSVM model. At the same time, an improved firefly algorithm is proposed to optimize the parameters of the
combined kernel function LSSVM. The final predictive value can be obtained by superimposing the predicted
value of each combined kernel function LSSVM prediction model. The actual collected short-term wind speed
data is chosen as the research object, the simulation experiments with four prediction horizons have been
implemented. Compared with state-of-the-art prediction methods, through the comparison result curve between
the prediction and actual wind speed, the box-plot results of predictive error distribution, the comparison
results of the relative prediction error, the performance indicators, the Pearson’s test, the DM test and the
Taylor diagram results show that the proposed prediction method has higher prediction accuracy and is able
to reflect the laws of wind speed correctly. Furthermore, the simulation results of four new datasets and adding
noise to the input data of training set show that the proposed prediction method has strong robustness.
1. Introduction
Electricity belongs to a market that involves generation, transmis-
sion and distribution agents as well as consumers, which desire to
maximize their profit and minimize expenses (Ribeiro et al., 2019).
Because of the current energy shortage in the world, the contradiction
between electricity supply and demand is prominent. Conventional
energy sources such as oil and coal face the problem of insufficient
reserves. As an important renewable natural energy, wind energy has
the advantages of huge reserves, renewability and pollution-free, so it
is recognized as an ideal renewable energy generation mode (Mishra
et al., 2018; Tian et al., 2018a,b). The output power of wind power
generation is closely related to wind speed of wind farm (Pradhan
and Bhende, 2019). Wind speed shows strong randomness and rapid
variation (Araghi et al., 2019). The accurate prediction of wind speed
in wind farms is of great practical significance for power departments to
adjust dispatching plans in time and to measure the capacity reliability
of wind farms (Murthy and Rahi, 2017; Vargas et al., 2019). Generally,

term and short-term (Wang et al., 2016). Long-term prediction is to
predict future wind speed in the next few years. Medium-term predic-
tion refers to the prediction of wind speed several days, weeks and
months in advance. Short-term wind speed prediction usually requires
1 to 48 h in advance to predict wind speed. Medium-term and long-
term wind speed prediction is mainly used for the evaluation of wind
resources in order to facilitate the planning and construction of wind
farms. Because of the randomness and uncertainty of wind speed, the
prediction of short-term wind speed has more theoretical and practical
value. Effective short-term wind speed prediction has important appli-
cation value for wind power generation. The main determinant of wind
power generation is local wind speed, so effective prediction of wind
speed is the key factor to predict wind power (Hu et al., 2018).
It is well known that wind speed is affected by many parameters
such as atmospheric pressure, temperature, humidity and etc. (Niau,
1995; Song et al., 2020). Therefore, if these environmental variables
can be reasonably introduced into the prediction model, the prediction

accuracy of short-term wind speed can be improved theoretically.
However, most of the current wind speed prediction methods only
use historical data of wind speed, rather than these environmental
variables. The main reasons are as follows.
1. Many new sensors are needed to measure these environmen-
tal variables. The installation, testing and data transmission of
sensors will increase the cost of wind speed acquisition system.
2. There is a certain coupling and correlation between these envi-
ronmental variables. If these environmental variables do not use
principal component analysis to extract principal components,
they will be used as input of prediction model, which will make
the information provided by these variables overlap to a certain
extent, so that the prediction accuracy will be reduced.
3. These environmental variables are the input of the prediction
model, which will increase the complexity of modeling, in-
crease the training time of the model, and reduce the real-time
performance of the prediction model.
At present, the commonly used wind speed prediction methods
include physical prediction method, persistence method, time series
method, Kalman filter, artificial neural network, fuzzy logic, deep learn-
ing machine, and combined prediction model, and etc. These research
methods are discussed in detail below.
1. Prediction models based on physical methods mainly include
numerical weather prediction (NWP) (Yang et al., 2018; Wang et al.,
2019a), spatial correlation method (Ye et al., 2017), etc. The prediction
model based on NWP can obtain wind speed prediction values for
the next 1 to 3 days. Its prediction accuracy is relatively stable, but
the calculation is huge. It often requires a huge computer to operate
continuously for hours, so it is not suitable for short-term wind speed
prediction. The spatial correlation method establishes a spatial correla-
tion model based on the wind speed data of wind stations around wind
farms to predict the wind speed in the coming hours. But, the spatial
correlation method is greatly affected by the location of wind stations
and the change of wind direction. Therefore, there are many limitations
in the application of prediction models based on physical methods.
2. The persistence method considers that the predictive wind speed
is equal to the sliding average value of the recent historical wind speed
values (Santamaria-Bonfil et al., 2016). Usually, the wind speed value
of the nearest sampling time is simply used as the wind speed prediction
value at the next sampling time. The prediction error of the persistence
method is large. And the predictive results are unstable.
3. Time series method uses a mass of historical data to build the
model. Through model recognition, parameter estimation and model
testing to determine a mathematical model that can describe the vari-
ation law of wind speed, and then deduces the prediction model to
achieve the purpose of prediction. Time series method include auto
regressive moving average (ARMA) model (Erdem and Shi, 2011), auto
regressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model (Cadenas et al.,
2016), auto-regressive integrated moving average with exogenous vari-
ables (ARIMAX) model (Yan et al., 2017), and etc. However, there are
some shortcomings, such as low prediction accuracy of low-order model
and difficulty in parameter estimation of high-order model.
4. The most typical advantage of Kalman filter prediction is that
it can correct the previous estimated value according to the latest
measured value, which has the characteristics of dynamic weighting
correction. Therefore, there are many short-term wind speed prediction
models based on Kalman filter (Galanis et al., 2017; Cai et al., 2019;
Zuluaga et al., 2015). In the calculation of observation vector and
state vector in Kalman filter model, it is necessary to assume that the
noise in the model is white noise with zero mean value. However, it is
difficult to accurately determine the statistical characteristics of noise
in the actual wind speed system. Because of the inaccuracy of the noise
characteristics, the Kalman filter model cannot accurately describe the
changing law of the wind speed system.
5. Artificial neural network is designed to imitate the structure
and function of human brain. It is composed of a large number of
simple processing elements connected in a large scale with a certain
topological structure. It has the characteristics of parallel processing,
distributed storage and fault tolerance, self-learning, self-organization,
self-adaptation, and can be used for short-term wind speed prediction
(Huseyin and Tansu, 2019). The typical used neural network for short-
term wind speed include radial basis function neural network (Chang
et al., 2017), fuzzy neural network (Ma et al., 2017), Elman neural
network (Yu et al., 2018, 2017), extreme learning machine (ELM) (Sun
et al., 2018; Luo et al., 2018; Tian et al., 2019), echo state network
(Chitsazan et al., 2019), wavelet neural network (Santhosh et al., 2018;
Wang et al., 2017), nonlinear neural network (Maruliya Begam and
Deepa, 2019; Liu et al., 2018), and etc. However, neural network has
inherent defects such as difficult to determine the network structure
scientifically, slow learning speed, existence of local optimal value,
memory instability and so on, which makes the prediction accuracy
difficult to guarantee. On the other hand, the training of neural network
needs a lot of sample data, which increase the computation time.
6. Fuzzy logic method uses fuzzy logic to form the professional
knowledge of engineers and technicians into a fuzzy rule base (An et al.,
2014; Khorramdel et al., 2018). Then a linear model is selected to ap-
proximate the wind speed with non-linear dynamic changes. However,
for wind speed prediction, the effect of fuzzy logic method is often
not good. This is mainly because the learning ability of fuzzy system
is weak, and the identification of fuzzy system has not yet formed a
perfect theory (Wang and Zhang, 2018). The process of fuzzification
and the assignment of fuzzy rules are lack of systematic methods, which
mainly rely on experience and trial implementation. Further research is
needed to determine the structure of the fuzzy system in the forecasting
system.
7. In recent years, many deep learning models are introduced to
predict wind speed. These models include long short-term memory
(LSTM) (Zhang et al., 2019a), convolutional neural networks (CNN)
(Zhou et al., 2018; Mi et al., 2019), recursive neural network (RNN) (Li
et al., 2019), and etc. However, deep learning models are very complex,
and they need a lot of computing resources to model. Although the
cost of calculation has been greatly reduced, the cost of calculation still
needs to be considered. For the simple problem of small data sets, with
the same computational overhead and time, deep learning models may
not produce enough additional effects than the model described above.
8. Other scholars try to use the combined model to predict wind
speed (Zhao et al., 2016; Kadhem et al., 2017; Wang and Li, 2019;
Jiang et al., 2018; Zhou et al., 2019a; Moreno and Coelho, 2018; Wang
et al., 2019b). The combined model is also named the hybrid or model.
At present, the combined model has been wildly used in many fields,
such as finances (Zhou et al., 2019b), agribusiness (Jimenez-Donaire
et al., 2020), health (Islam et al., 2019), industry (Wang et al., 2019d;
Han et al., 2019), and etc. In these fields, the combined models often
achieve better predictive performance than single models. Therefore,
it is very important to study and apply the combined model. In the
combined model, the advantages of different prediction models are
combined, and good prediction results are achieved. However, it is
difficult to determine the appropriate combined prediction model and
the weight coefficients of each prediction model (Wang et al., 2019c;
Bokde et al., 2019). At the same time, compared with the single
prediction model, the advantages of the combined prediction model
are difficult to prove and analyze in theory (Zhang et al., 2019b).
Therefore, it is not guaranteed that the performance of the combined
prediction model is better than that of the single prediction model.
In summary, most of these prediction methods are aimed at the
original wind speed series, and the average relative prediction error
usually reaches about 10% to 20%. Obviously, the limited short-term
wind speed data itself cannot completely reproduce all the character-
istics of the wind system, but these observed wind speed data can be
regarded as a kind of signal, which can be processed to obtain a lot of

useful information. Because wind speed is influenced by temperature,
air pressure, topography and other factors, it has strong randomness
and contains very rich characteristic information. By preprocessing the
original wind speed series, the information of different characteristics is
decomposed. This will reduce the difficulty of modeling and hopefully
improve the prediction accuracy. Local mean decomposition (LMD)
proposed in 2005 provide a good solution to the problem of information
extraction in the original signal (Smith, 2005). LMD is highly adaptive.
It can decompose any complex non-stationary signal to multiple and
physically meaningful production function (PF) components (Jia et al.,
2019). Then the instantaneous frequency and amplitude of the obtained
PF component are combined to obtain the complete information distri-
bution of the original signal (Yu and Lv, 2017). If the factors affecting
wind speed and their influencing rules remain basically unchanged, the
PF components obtained by LMD decomposition can better describe
the time evolution law of one or more of the influencing wind speed
changes. Therefore, LMD can lay a good foundation for extracting the
relevant information of the internal variation law of wind speed.
In 2000, based on support vector machine (SVM), least squares
support vector machine (LSSVM) was proposed. LSSVM transforms the
quadratic programming problem in SVM into solving linear equations,
which reduces the complexity of solving. Therefore, LSSVM is very
suitable for short-term wind speed prediction and has achieved some
research results (Wang et al., 2018; Xiang et al., 2019). One of the
greatest advantages of LSSVM algorithm is that it needs fewer samples
and ensures higher prediction accuracy (Chen et al., 2019). In practical
application, the samples of short-term wind speed are sometimes diffi-
cult to obtain or there are many unqualified samples, so the sample
size is very small. Therefore, the practicability of LSSVM has more
advantages than neural network, deep learning model, and etc. The
combination of the decomposed PF component and the small sample
advantage of LSSVM model can fully explore the physical mechanism
and laws contained in the short-term wind speed data itself, which is
also in line with the mechanism of using data self-driving to obtain
the influencing factors, thus laying a good foundation for improving
the prediction accuracy of short-term wind speed. However, the pre-
diction accuracy of LSSVM is affected by the kernel function and the
parameters of the kernel function (Liu et al., 2017). At present, there
is no definite theory and method to support how to determine the
kernel function and the parameters of the kernel function. In order to
improve the prediction accuracy of LSSVM and solve the problem of
selecting the kernel function and the parameters of the kernel function
in LSSVM algorithm, this paper uses global kernel function and local
kernel function to construct the combined kernel function. The global
kernel function is used to fit the distant correlation in the sample, and
the local kernel function is used to approximate the correlation in the
adjacent data domain, so as to improve the generalization ability of
the LSSVM model. In order to determine the optimal parameters of the
combined kernel function LSSVM, an improved firefly algorithm (FA) is
proposed to optimize the parameters. This improved FA improves the
weight update strategy of standard FA to accelerate the convergence
speed of the population and reduce the impact of randomness on the
performance of the algorithm.
Based on the above description, this paper first uses LMD to pro-
cess the short-term wind speed, and obtains the PF components and
residual component of the original short-term wind speed series. Then,
each PF component and residual component is trained and predicted
by combined kernel function LSSVM model. The parameters of each
combined kernel function LSSVM model are optimized by improved FA.
Finally, the prediction results of different PF components and residual
component are superimposed to generate final short-term wind speed
prediction values.
The main innovations and research ideas of this paper are given.
1. LMD is introduced to obtain the PF components and residual
component of original short-term wind speed time series.

2. The combined kernel function LSSVM model is proposed to
improve the prediction ability. The combined kernel function LSSVM
is chosen as the prediction model of each PF and residual component.
3. An improved FA is proposed to optimize the parameters of
combined kernel function LSSVM model.
Compared with traditional prediction models such as neural net-
work and time series, and modern computational intelligence tools such
as LSTM and CNN, the advantages of the proposed prediction method
are summarized as follows.
1. The algorithm of the proposed prediction method is LSSVM.
Therefore, the prediction method needs fewer samples and has
more advantages in practice. This is the main advantage of the
proposed prediction method.
2. Compared with the deep learning model and the neural network,
the training time of the prediction method in this paper is less.
3. The combined kernel function LSSVM model has low dependence
on single kernel functions and their parameters, and has high model-
ing accuracy. Combined with improved FA, it is more reasonable to
determine the parameters of the prediction model.
4. LMD can effectively explain the fluctuation, periodicity and trend
of short-term wind speed.

2. Basic theories
In this section, the required theories that are applied in the devel-
oped prediction framework are introduced as follows.
2.1. LMD
LMD is a nonlinear signal analysis method proposed in 2005. Its
essence is to decompose the signal adaptively into the sum of a series of
PF components with physical significance, thus reflecting the intrinsic
nature of the signal and obtaining the time–frequency distribution of
the original signal. Many signals in practical engineering applications
are nonlinear and non-stationary. Using the ensemble decomposition
method can reduce the non-stationary of the signal and extract the
information of different frequency. On the basis of this, the ensemble
decomposition method is combined with some prediction methods or
prediction models can improve the prediction effect and achieve better
performance index than single model. In these ensemble decomposition
methods, LMD, empirical mode decomposition (EMD), ensemble em-
pirical mode decomposition (EEMD), complementary empirical mode
decomposition (CEEMD) are typical representatives. Compared with
EMD, EEMD and CEEMD, LMD has some unique advantages. EMD has
the phenomenon of end point overlapping. EEMD and CEMD add the
white noise in the original signal, which will increase the calculation
time. LMD can decompose the signal adaptively according to its own
characteristics, so that each component after decomposition has a
certain physical significance, and can reflect the inherent nature of the
signal, which provides a good foundation for other post-processing of
the signal. At the same time, LMD has some advantages in restrain-
ing the end effect, reducing the calculation time and preserving the
integrity of signal information.

The introduction of kernel function avoids the complex calcula-
tion in high dimensional feature space, but different kernel functions
achieve the different performance. The choice of kernel function be-
comes one of the core problems of LSSVM. The partial kernel function
has a great influence on the data points in the small area near the test
point, so it has strong learning ability, but the generalization ability is
weak. The characteristics of global kernel function are just the opposite.
That is meant the partial kernel function has strong learning ability
and weak generalization performance, while global kernel function has
strong generalization performance and weak learning ability. There-
fore, we can consider the advantages of combining these two kinds of
kernel functions, and construct the mixed-kernel function.
In the literature (Smits and Jordaan, 2002), the author points out
that the Polynomial kernel function is a global kernel function with
global characteristics and good generalization ability. The sample point
is far away from the test point will also affect the output of the function.
As a kind of partial kernel function, the parameter 𝜎2 of RBF determine
the width of the kernel function. Only the sample point close to the
test point has an effect on the output of the function, so RBF function
has partial characteristics and good interpolation ability. Therefore, in
order to make the learning ability and generalization ability of LSSVM
better, these two kernel functions can be combined to construct a
combined kernel function. The advantages of two kernel functions are
combined. Better regression prediction performance can be obtained.

modeling process is the same, but the difference is that the parameters
of different prediction models are generated after training.
The number of decomposition layers k of LMD is also an important
parameter. The larger the value of k is, the higher the complexity of
the model. However, unlike EMD or EEMD, the decomposition level of
LMD is determined by the characteristics of the signal itself. Through
the iterative algorithm, different PF components are obtained until the
termination condition is satisfied. Therefore, k does not need to be
specified in the algorithm. Generally speaking, the decomposition level
of LMD is less than EMD or EEMD, resulting in faster calculation time
(Xie et al., 2016).

5.2. Discussion II: the association strength
In this section, the discussion of association strength based on

developed prediction method compared with other models. In detail,
if Pearson’s correlation coefficient is equal to 1, it indicates that the

5.3. Discussion III: the statistical significance
The statistical significance of the proposed prediction method is
discussed to prove superiority in short-term wind speed prediction
from the point of statistics. The DM test based on the square error
loss function is used to show the significance of the superiority of the
proposed prediction method compared with other models. The results
for the DM test are listed in Tables 9–12, which indicates that the DM
test values of all compared models are greater than the critical value
of the 1%, 5%, and 10% significance level. Therefore, we can reject
the null hypothesis at the 1%, 5%, and 10% significance level, and we
believe that the proposed prediction method significantly outperforms
all compared models. Therefore, we can reasonably draw the conclu-
sion that the proposed prediction method not only achieves higher
prediction accuracy, but also shows a significant difference in terms
of the prediction accuracy level, which further proves the superiority
of the developed proposed prediction method in short-term wind speed
prediction.

5.5. Discussion V: the advantages of the proposed method
From the above discussion, we can know that the proposed predic-
tion method has achieved better results. According to Discussions I,
II, III, and IV, we can safely draw the conclusion that the proposed
prediction method shows a more powerful forecasting ability than
the compared models. The main advantages of the proposed method
in relation to compared models are as follows. (a) The introduction
of LMD. After LMD processing, each component after decomposition
contains basically the same deformation information, which reduces
the interference between different information in modeling process.
The prediction difficulty and complexity are both reduced. (b) The
proposed combined kernel function LSSVM model has low dependence
on single kernel functions and their parameters, and has high modeling
accuracy. Combined with developed improved FA, the combined kernel
function LSSVM can better describe the change law of the prediction
object. (c) Because the developed prediction model is derived from the
improvement of LSSVM, it inherits the advantages of LSSVM. Namely,
the modeling process needs little sample data. This is very useful for
the research object with limited sample size in practical application.

6. Conclusion
In this paper, LMD algorithm is used to decompose the original
short-term wind speed time series. The PF components and residual
component of different scales can be obtained, which simplifies the cou-
pling between different feature information and reduces the difficulty
of prediction and modeling. The combined kernel function is selected
as the kernel function of LSSSVM. The global kernel function is used to
fit the correlation of the distant sample data. The generalization perfor-
mance of the LSSVM model is improved. An improved FA with better
convergence performance is introduced to optimize the parameters of
combined kernel function LSSVM. The proposed prediction method is
applied to the multi-step prediction of short-term wind speed time
series collected from a wind farm, and compared with other prediction
methods. The main results of this study are as the follows. (a) Compared
with other state-of-the-art models, the proposed prediction method has
better performance indicators. It shows that the proposed prediction
method can better fit the short-term wind speed data. (b) From the
statistical perspective, the DM test shows that the proposed prediction
method significantly outperforms the other comparative models at
different significance levels. (c) The Pearson’s test of the proposed
prediction method is higher than those of other comparative models.
(d) The result of Taylor diagram indicates that the proposed method
has smaller correlation coefficient as the observation. (e) Through two
case studies, the robustness of the proposed prediction method is also
verified. In a conclusion, the proposed prediction method is effective.
The short-term wind speed prediction method proposed in this
paper has good application value in the engineering practice of wind
system. However, the traditional LMD employs the moving average
method to obtain the local mean function and local envelope function,
which cause the over-smoothness easily and affects the precision of
decomposition. Therefore, in the future, this paper will further study
the improvement of LMD method to achieve accurate decomposition
of short-term wind speed time series.
